Priya / Sarah — quick triage notes (ops):

- Observed signal: p95 went from ~230ms to ~610ms; p99 from ~480ms to ~1.3s in your hotpath traces. 5xx rose to ~3.8% concentrated on the tokenization/encoder stage.
- Root candidate: v5b-int8 changed the kernel path for QKV attention and reduced L2 cache locality for longer sequences. This increases KV cache misses on hot sessions and forces more CPU-GPU syncs for prefix handling.
- Also seeing an uptick in generation divergence for prompts that regularly hit long-context state (your underwriting templates). Likely quant-induced numeric variance; hallucination reports match tokens where logits changed most.

Immediate mitigations we've executed in parallel (10:00 - 10:12 PT):
- Canary rollback prepared: model v5a-fp16 image verified and warm.
- Traffic split: we routed 30% of traffic back to v5a-fp16 for a small subset of hotpath routes (underwriting.request.*) — p99 on that slice dropped to ~360ms and 5xx ~0.5% after warm-up.
- Enabled prefix/KV aggressive caching for your customer namespace to reduce repeated KV misses.

Next steps (actionable):
1) If Bridgecrest approves, we'll flip 100% traffic to v5a-fp16 for the underwriting hotpath and keep v5b-int8 off for 24h while we collect diffs.
2) Run a short evaluation harness on the attached failing examples to generate a differential report (accuracy/hallucination delta) — ETA 90 mins.
3) Engineering will instrument additional per-token debug logs for the worst-case prompts and share redacted outputs.

If you want the full rollback now, say the word and we'll cutover. Otherwise we'll continue phased rollback and monitor.

Subject: Bridgecrest — executive summary & next steps (hotline call scheduled)

Sarah / Adam —

Thank you for your patience. Quick executive summary and asks before our 14:00 PT hotline call:

What happened:
- v5b-int8 rollout introduced kernel/quantization paths that increased KV cache misses on long-context hotpaths. This produced higher tail latency and numeric divergence on a small set of underwriting prompts, yielding incorrect extractions.

What we did so far (completed):
- Phased rollback on underwriting routes to v5a-fp16 (now 100% for underwriting.request.*).
- Aggressive prefix/KV caching enabled for Bridgecrest namespace.
- Short differential eval completed on 200 sample prompts; initial report attached (MAP doc).

Current status:
- Throughput for the underwriting batch window is restored; p99 reduced from 1.3s -> ~380ms on the rollback slice. 5xx dropped to ~0.4% on the hotpath.
- We still see a small class of prompts with subtle token-level variance; engineering will run extended synthetic tests and provide a definitive pass/fail matrix within 90–120 minutes.

Requests / Next steps:
1) Approve 24-hour hold on v5b-int8 for Bridgecrest production while we finish investigations and build a safe remediation (tuning qprofile or targeted kernel fix).
2) Accept MAP deliverable and remediation timeline (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MAP-Bridgecrest).
3) Exec call at 14:00 PT — I'll chair; Hannah will cover credits and SLA mitigation if needed.

Sarah, please confirm approval for the 24-hour hold and if you'd like us to open a formal RCA ticket with your security/contact info included.

—Priya
